core_obligations: From quasi-compactness to finite subcoverings (proof lines 3534-3554): the identity of the object is a section of the sheaf represented by it, so after refining a covering it comes from a single summand of the coproduct; quasi-compactness then produces a covering whose indexing has finite image, and the corresponding finite set of summands already surjects.

From finite subcoverings to quasi-compactness (proof lines 3556-3578): given a covering of the object, the induced map from the coproduct of the representable sheaves of its members onto the representable sheaf is a surjection; the hypothesis provides a finite subfamily which still surjects, and a section argument produces members of the original covering whose images cover the object.
proof_roadmap: Follow the identity section through a coproduct of sheaves to reduce it to finitely many summands.
Conversely, turn a covering into a surjection from a coproduct of representables and apply the finite subcovering hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes quasi-compact objects of a site by a finiteness property of surjections onto the sheaf represented by the object: such a surjection from a coproduct of sheaves admits a finite subfamily which is still surjective (statement lines 3520-3531). The proof is a complete equivalence: the first implication follows the identity section through the description of a coproduct of sheaves as a sheafified coproduct, refines the covering and uses quasi-compactness to obtain a covering with finite image, which yields the finite subfamily (proof lines 3534-3554); the converse turns a covering into a surjection from a coproduct of representable sheaves, applies the hypothesis to get a finite subfamily and produces the required members by a section argument (proof lines 3556-3578). The non-formal content is the passage between sections of a coproduct and single summands. The claim is H2: two written-out implications with each input named.
